questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

The doctor knew that Ravindra would recover from dengue soon and do the kind of work he __was doing__ before.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**had been doing**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 

__
 
• The sentence is in the past tense, indicating that the doctor already knew something before.
 
• "**Had been doing**" is the **past perfect continuous tense**, indicating that Ravindra was doing a certain kind of work before he got sick.
 
• The structure should be: Subject + had been + present participle (verb + ing)__
 
• This tense is appropriate because it shows that Ravindra was doing the work for a period of time before he got sick and that he may continue doing it after he recovers.
 
• The use of "**had been doing**" implies a continuous action or state in the past, emphasizing the ongoing nature of the work. 

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

**Corrected sentence**: *The doctor knew that Ravindra would recover from dengue soon and do the kind of work he had been doing before.*

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into four parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.**

The English / often / fought / French.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error is in the subject of the sentence, which should be "**The French**" instead of "**French**".
 
• The definite article "**The**" is needed before "French" to make it a specific group of people.
 
• "French" can also be used as an adjective, but in this case, it needs to modify a noun, such as "French soldiers".

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

**Corrected sentence**: *The English often fought the French.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the following sentence in active voice.**

Why is the rotten apple being eaten by you?

options.text: Why were you eating the rotten apple?
Why you are eating the rotten apple?
Why have you eaten the rotten apple?
Why are you eating the rotten apple?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**Why are you eating the rotten apple?**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 

__
 
• The sentence is in passive voice, with the subject (**rotten apple**) being acted upon by the verb (**being eaten**) and the object (**you**) doing the action.
 
• **Passive voice structure**: Why + is/am/are + subject + being + past participle of the main verb + by + agent (optional)?__
 
• To change it to active voice, we need to make the subject (**you**) the doer of the action and the object (**rotten apple**) the recipient of the action.
 
• **Active voice structure**: __Why + present tense of the verb to be + subject + present participle (verb + ing) + object?__
 
• The correct active voice sentence would be "*Why are you eating the rotten apple?*"

Thus, **option 4** is the correct answer.

questions.question: **Select the option that expresses the following sentence in positive degree of comparison. Istanbul is a beautiful city.**

options.text: The city of Istanbul is as beautiful as other cities.
Istanbul is a very beautiful city.
No other place I have seen is as beautiful as Istanbul.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**No other place I have seen is as beautiful as Istanbul.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The original sentence "**Istanbul is a beautiful city**" is a positive statement describing the beauty of Istanbul.
 
• To express this in the positive degree of comparison, we use the structure "**more + adjective + than**" when comparing to other places.
 
• Therefore, "*No place I have seen is more beautiful than Istanbul*" conveys the idea that, among the places the speaker has visited, Istanbul is the most beautiful.
 
• This construction emphasizes the positive quality of Istanbul's beauty without making a direct comparison to other places.
 
• The positive degree is achieved by using "**more**" followed by the adjective ("**beautiful**") and "**than**" to indicate the comparison.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

• The verb "**think**" is used to express thoughts or opinions.
 
• In this sentence, the speaker is expressing their thought about taking their belongings to the new apartment tomorrow.
 
• The original sentence is grammatically incorrect. The error lies in the use of "**have**" before "**think**."
 
• The verb "**have**" is not needed in this context.
